concept.name: Delta divergence
concept.definition: A mismatch between price direction and volume delta: for example, price printing a new high while bar delta or cumulative delta fails to make a corresponding new high, indicating that the aggressive order flow no longer supports the price move. Practitioners read it as a warning of weakening initiative or active absorption by the passive side.
concept.intuition: If price keeps climbing but buyers are swinging less hard each push, someone on the other side may be quietly absorbing their market orders.
concept.mechanics: Successive price extremes are compared with the corresponding delta or CVD extremes; divergence is flagged when the price extreme is not matched by a delta extreme, often explained by large resting limit orders absorbing market orders so that aggression produces little price progress.
concept.failure_modes: Delta can diverge for long stretches while the trend continues, and on low-quality data feeds misclassified trades fabricate divergence; the pattern is frequent and far from decisive on its own.
concept.misconceptions: Delta divergence is not proof of hidden institutional intent — it is equally consistent with ordinary passive liquidity, and it is an observation to be confirmed, not a stand-alone entry signal.
concept.example: ES pushes to a new session high while the bar's delta prints well below the prior high's delta; the footprint shows big ask volume absorbed at the offer, and price subsequently rotates down.
